apps.allow_client_commands_desc: Whether to execute client prepare commands when running this app.
apps.app_name_desc: The name your devices show for this app
apps.applications_desc: The apps and games your devices can launch.
apps.applications_reorder_desc: Drag to reorder. Saving any change ends the app that is currently running.
apps.applications_tips: Right-click an app's launch button to copy a link that starts it on a paired device. Double-click an app's name to export it for an emulator frontend.
apps.auto_detach: Continue streaming if the application exits quickly
apps.auto_detach_desc: This will attempt to automatically detect launcher-type apps that close quickly after launching another program or instance of themselves. When a launcher-type app is detected, it is treated as a detached app.
apps.close_warning: Are you sure to terminate the current running app?
apps.cmd_desc: The main application to start. If blank, no application will be started.
apps.cmd_note: If the path to the command executable contains spaces, you must enclose it in quotes.
apps.cmd_prep_desc: A list of commands to be run before/after this application. If any of the prep-commands fail, starting the application is aborted.
apps.cmd_state_desc:
A list of commands to be run when resuming(first client connects when no clients are connected) or pausing(all clients disconnect) this application.
Do commands for resume and Undo command for pause.
Please make sure to clean up any side effects of the commands in the preparation undo commands.
Please note that pause command will not be executed when the session terminates.
apps.detached_cmds_desc: A list of commands to be run in the background.
apps.detached_cmds_note: If the path to the command executable contains spaces, you must enclose it in quotes.
apps.env_client_audio_config: The Audio Configuration requested by the client (2.0/5.1/7.1)
apps.env_client_enable_sops: The client has requested the option to optimize the game for optimal streaming (true/false)
apps.env_client_fps: The FPS requested by the client (float)
apps.env_client_gcmap: The requested gamepad mask, in a bitset/bitfield format (int)
apps.env_client_hdr: HDR is enabled by the client (true/false)
apps.env_client_height: The Height requested by the client (int)
apps.env_client_host_audio: The client has requested host audio (true/false)
apps.env_client_name: Name of the client starting the stream (string)
apps.env_client_uuid: UUID of the client starting the stream (string)
apps.env_client_width: The Width requested by the client (int)
apps.env_tunastream_compatibility: TUNASTREAM_CLIENT_FPS can be a decimal such as 59.940. If a tool needs a whole number, turn on ENVVAR compatibility mode in Configuration.
apps.env_vars_desc: All commands get these environment variables by default:
apps.exit_timeout_desc: Number of seconds to wait for all app processes to gracefully exit when requested to quit. If unset, the default is to wait up to 5 seconds. If set to zero or a negative value, the app will be immediately terminated.
apps.global_prep_desc: Enable/Disable the execution of Global Prep Commands for this application.
apps.global_state_desc: Enable/Disable the execution of Global Resume/Pause Commands for this application.
apps.image_desc: Application icon/picture/image path that will be sent to client. Image must be a PNG file. If not set, TunaStream will send default box image.
apps.launch_local_client: Do you want to launch the app from local client on this device?
apps.launch_warning: Are you sure you want to launch this app? This will terminate the currently running app.
apps.name: Name
apps.output_desc: The file where the output of the command is stored, if it is not specified, the output is ignored
apps.per_client_app_identity_desc: Separate the app's identity per-client. Useful when you want different virtual display configurations on this specific app for different clients
apps.picker_failed: Something went wrong. Try again, or add the app by hand.
apps.picker_lead: These are installed on this PC. Tick the ones you want to start from your devices, then add them. Games open through their own launcher, just as they would if you started them on the PC.
apps.picker_loading: Looking for games and programs on this PC. This can take a few seconds…
apps.picker_none: No games or programs were found. You can still add one by hand with Add app.
apps.picker_running: A game is running. End the session from the home page before adding apps.
apps.picker_title: Add games and programs from this PC
apps.resolution_scale_factor_desc: Scale the client requested resolution based on this factor. e.g. 2000x1000 with a factor of 120% will become 2400x1200. Overrides client requested factor when the number isn't 100%. This option won't affect client requested streaming resolution.
apps.run_as_desc: This can be necessary for some applications that require administrator permissions to run properly. Might cause URL schemes to fail.
apps.site_bad: That doesn't look like a web address. It should look like https://www.example.com.
apps.site_lead: Starting it from a TV or phone opens the site in this PC's own browser, signed in as you are here. With TunaReceive's picture-in-picture, you can watch it in a corner of the TV over another app. Ending the session leaves the browser open on the PC.
apps.terminate_on_pause_desc: Terminate the app when all clients are disconnected.
apps.use_app_identity_desc: Use the app's own identity while creating virtual displays instead of client's. This is useful when you want display configuration for each APP separately.
apps.virtual_display_desc: Always create a virtual display when starting this app, overriding client request. Please make sure the SudoVDA driver is installed and enabled.
apps.virtual_display_primary_desc: Automatically set the virtual display as primary display when the app starts. Virtual display will always be set to primary when client requests to use virtual display. (Recommended to keep on) [Broken on Windows 11 24H2]
apps.wait_all: Continue streaming until all app processes exit
apps.wait_all_desc: This will continue streaming until all processes started by the app have terminated. When unchecked, streaming will stop when the initial app process exits, even if other app processes are still running.
apps.working_dir_desc: The working directory that should be passed to the process. For example, some applications use the working directory to search for configuration files. If not set, TunaStream will default to the parent directory of the command
apps.sync_desc: Adds the games you've played lately, from Steam, Epic, GOG, EA, Ubisoft, Amazon and the Microsoft Store, with their covers. Steam says when each game was last played; for the others TunaStream asks Windows when the game last ran. Games are removed again when uninstalled or not played for that long. Apps you added yourself are never touched, and a synced game you delete stays deleted. Nothing changes while someone is streaming.
apps.sync_excluded: {n} synced games you deleted stay off the list.
apps.sync_badge_title: Added by Keep my games in sync

client_card.clients_desc: Clients that are specifically tuned to work the best with TunaStream
client_card.generic_moonlight_clients_desc: Moonlight and other compatible apps work with TunaStream too.

config.adapter_name_desc_linux_1: Manually specify a GPU to use for capture.
config.adapter_name_desc_linux_2: to find all devices capable of VAAPI
config.adapter_name_desc_linux_3: Replace ``renderD129`` with the device from above to lists the name and capabilities of the device. To be supported by TunaStream, it needs to have at the very minimum:
config.adapter_name_desc_windows: Manually specify a GPU to use for capture. If unset, the GPU is chosen automatically. We strongly recommend leaving this field blank to use automatic GPU selection! Note: This GPU must have a display connected and powered on. The appropriate values can be found using the following command:
config.address_family_desc: Whether to accept connections over IPv6 as well as IPv4. Leave on IPv4 only unless you know you need IPv6.
config.advanced_desc: Most people never need these. Change them only if you are fixing a specific problem.
config.always_send_scancodes_desc: Helps games that ignore typed keys. Turn off if the wrong characters appear when your device uses a keyboard layout other than US English.
config.amd_coder_desc: Allows you to select the entropy encoding to prioritize quality or encoding speed. H.264 only.
config.amd_enforce_hrd_desc: Increases the constraints on rate control to meet HRD model requirements. This greatly reduces bitrate overflows, but may cause encoding artifacts or reduced quality on certain cards.
config.amd_preanalysis_desc: This enables rate-control preanalysis, which may increase quality at the expense of increased encoding latency.
config.amd_quality_desc: This controls the balance between encoding speed and quality.
config.amd_rc_cbr: cbr -- constant bitrate (recommended if HRD is enabled)
config.amd_rc_desc: This controls the rate control method to ensure we are not exceeding the client bitrate target. 'cqp' is not suitable for bitrate targeting, and other options besides 'vbr_latency' depend on HRD Enforcement to help constrain bitrate overflows.
config.amd_rc_vbr_latency: vbr_latency -- latency constrained variable bitrate (recommended if HRD is disabled; default)
config.amd_usage_desc: This sets the base encoding profile. All options presented below will override a subset of the usage profile, but there are additional hidden settings applied that cannot be configured elsewhere.
config.amd_vbaq_desc: The human visual system is typically less sensitive to artifacts in highly textured areas. In VBAQ mode, pixel variance is used to indicate the complexity of spatial textures, allowing the encoder to allocate more bits to smoother areas. Enabling this feature leads to improvements in subjective visual quality with some content.
config.apply_note: Click 'Apply' to restart TunaStream and apply changes. This will terminate any running sessions.
config.audio_sink_desc_linux: The name of the audio sink used for Audio Loopback. If you do not specify this variable, pulseaudio will select the default monitor device. You can find the name of the audio sink using either command:
config.audio_sink_desc_macos: The name of the audio sink used for Audio Loopback. TunaStream can only access microphones on macOS due to system limitations. To stream system audio using Soundflower or BlackHole.
config.audio_sink_desc_windows:
The audio device to be used when audio output is allowed on host by the client.
If unset, the device is chosen automatically.
You can get the Device ID using the following command:
config.auto_capture_sink_desc: Auto capture current sink after default audio sink changed.
config.av1_mode_desc: The newest video format, sharper still on graphics cards that support it (NVIDIA RTX 40, AMD RX 7000, Intel Arc and newer). Automatic offers it when your graphics card supports it.
config.back_button_timeout: Hold Back/Select for the Guide button
config.back_button_timeout_desc: For controllers without a Guide (Xbox/PS) button: holding Back/Select this many milliseconds presses it. -1 turns this off.
config.capture_desc: Automatic uses the first method that works.
config.capture_wgc_desc: Windows.Graphics.Capture can be smoother with games that use frame generation or run in windows, and costs a little more graphics power. TunaStream captures through a small helper in your signed-in session, and switches to Desktop Duplication by itself when nobody is signed in, during UAC prompts and on the lock screen. Go back to Automatic if anything looks wrong.
config.cert_desc: Used to secure this page and pairing. TunaStream makes one for you; it should use an RSA-2048 key.
config.channels_desc_1: TunaStream can allow a single streaming session to be shared with multiple clients simultaneously.
config.channels_desc_2: Some hardware encoders may have limitations that reduce performance with multiple streams.
config.coder_cabac: cabac -- context adaptive binary arithmetic coding - higher quality
config.coder_cavlc: cavlc -- context adaptive variable-length coding - faster decode
config.controller_desc: Let devices use a game controller on this PC.
config.credentials_file_desc: Where the web interface username and password are kept.
config.dd_config_ensure_only_display: Deactivate other displays and activate only the specified display
config.dd_config_ensure_primary: Activate the display automatically and make it a primary display
config.dd_config_revert_delay_desc: Additional delay in milliseconds to wait before reverting configuration when the app has been closed or the last session terminated. Main purpose is to provide a smoother transition when quickly switching between apps.
config.dd_config_revert_on_disconnect_desc: Revert configuration upon disconnect of all clients instead of app close or last session termination.
config.dd_config_verify_only: Verify that the display is enabled
config.dd_hdr_option_auto: Switch on/off the HDR mode as requested by the client (default)
config.dd_mode_remapping_desc_1: Specify remapping entries to change the requested resolution and/or refresh rate to other values.
config.dd_mode_remapping_desc_2: The list is iterated from top to bottom and the first match is used.
config.dd_mode_remapping_desc_3: "Requested" fields can be left empty to match any requested value.
config.dd_mode_remapping_desc_4_final_values_mi: At least one "Final" field must be specified. The unspecified resolution or refresh rate will not be changed.
config.dd_mode_remapping_desc_4_final_values_no: "Final" field must be specified and cannot be empty.
config.dd_mode_remapping_desc_5_sops_mixed_only: "Optimize game settings" option must be turned on in the app on the device, otherwise entries with any resolution fields specified are skipped.
config.dd_mode_remapping_desc_5_sops_resolution: "Optimize game settings" option must be turned on in the app on the device, otherwise the mapping is skipped.
config.dd_refresh_rate_option_auto: Use FPS value provided by the client (default)
config.dd_refresh_rate_option_manual_desc: Enter the refresh rate to be used
config.dd_resolution_option_auto: Use resolution provided by the client (default)
config.dd_resolution_option_manual_desc: Enter the resolution to be used
config.dd_resolution_option_multi_instance_desc: When using multiple instance of TunaStream, make sure you have disabled this option in all instances, or it'll end up messing things up. It's still recommended to disable this part if you don't want your physical monitor's resolution to change or you only stream with virtual display.
config.dd_resolution_option_ogs_desc: "Optimize game settings" option must be turned on in the app on the device for this to work.
config.dd_resolution_option_vdisplay_desc: Not recommended to use this option on usual circumstances. Please use native Windows settings to change display configurations. When using virtual display, only built-in resolution and client requested resolution/refresh rate will work.
config.dd_wa_hdr_toggle_delay_desc_1: When using virtual display device (VDD) for streaming, it might incorrectly display HDR color. TunaStream can try to mitigate this issue, by turning HDR off and then on again.
config.dd_wa_hdr_toggle_delay_desc_2: If the value is set to 0, the workaround is disabled (default). If the value is between 0 and 3000 milliseconds, TunaStream will turn off HDR, wait for the specified amount of time and then turn HDR on again. The recommended delay time is around 500 milliseconds in most cases.
config.dd_wa_hdr_toggle_delay_desc_3: DO NOT use this workaround unless you actually have issues with HDR as it directly impacts stream start time!
config.double_refreshrate: Run the stream's screen at double speed
config.double_refreshrate_desc: Can smooth out stutter on some PCs. The stream itself is not affected.
config.ds4_back_as_touchpad_click_desc: For controllers without a touchpad: pressing Back/Select acts as a touchpad click on the PlayStation 4 controller.
config.enable_discovery: Let devices find this PC on their own
config.enable_discovery_desc: Your PC shows up by itself in TunaReceive (and Moonlight) on the same network. Turn off to hide it; devices then need the PC's IP address to add it.
config.enable_input_only_mode: Add a "Control only" entry to the app list
config.enable_input_only_mode_desc: Adds an entry that sends your controller, mouse and keyboard to the PC without any picture or sound, for using a device as a remote while you watch the PC's own screen.
config.enable_pairing_desc: Turn off once all your devices are paired so nobody else can add one. Devices already paired keep working.
config.encoder_desc: Automatic uses your graphics card. Choose one only if streaming fails to start; a hardware encoder must be on the graphics card your monitor is plugged into. Software works on any PC but uses a lot of CPU.
config.end_session_on_disconnect: Quit the game when the last device disconnects
config.end_session_on_disconnect_desc: Off: the game keeps running after you close the stream, so you can pick up where you left off. On: closing the stream also closes the game and gives your screen back right away. Either way, if the connection drops (a Wi-Fi hiccup, a device going to sleep) the game keeps running for two minutes so you can reconnect.
config.envvar_compatibility_mode_desc: Gives commands TUNASTREAM_CLIENT_FPS as a whole number instead of a decimal such as 59.940, for tools that cannot read decimals.
config.experts_note: Most people never need to change anything here. TunaStream picks good values on its own, and a wrong value can stop streaming from working. If something breaks after a change, clear the field to go back to the default.
config.external_ip_desc: Only for streaming away from home. Leave empty to detect it automatically.
config.fallback_mode_desc: TunaStream will use this mode when the client does not provide a mode or when the app is launched through the web UI. Format: [Width]x[Height]x[FPS]
config.ui_theme_seasonal_desc: Halloween colours in October, autumn in November, winter from December to mid-January and summer in July and August, then back to your theme. TunaReceive follows when it matches the PC.
config.shared_pc_borderless_desc: In many games, full screen means the PC's main monitor. Set the game to Windowed in its own settings instead: TunaStream takes off its border and stretches it over the TV's screen, so it looks full screen there while your monitors stay yours. Only the game's own window is changed, once it has kept the TV's shape (16:9) for 3 seconds; launchers and dialogs are left alone. Nothing is done inside the game. For the sharpest picture, set the game's resolution to the TV's.
config.quiet_notifications_desc: Turns on Windows' Do not disturb while a stream runs, so notifications don't pop up over the game (they still collect in the notification centre), and turns it off again afterwards. If it was already on, it is left alone. In Shared PC mode this also silences notifications for you at the PC.
config.shared_pc_tv_primary: Make the TV's screen the main one
config.shared_pc_tv_primary_desc: Games then open on the TV by themselves, at the TV's resolution, which suits games that insist on full screen on the main display. New windows you open that land on the TV's screen are moved to the screen your mouse is on. Your own windows from Windows (File Explorer, Settings, Task Manager, dialogs) move too. Notifications appear on the main screen, so turn on Do not disturb during streams to keep them off the TV; the main taskbar and its clock, and the "Do you want to allow" (UAC) prompt, stay on the TV, because Windows draws them only on the main screen.
config.shared_pc: Keep using this PC while someone streams
config.shared_pc_desc: Your monitor stays the main screen, so your windows, taskbar and notifications stay with you; only the streamed game's windows go to the TV. Only the game's sound goes to the stream, and your sound stays on your speakers. Your mouse can't wander onto the TV's screen. Windows still has one keyboard focus: clicking your own windows can make some games pause or stop reading the controller. When the controller is in use and you haven't touched your mouse or keyboard for 8 seconds, the game gets focus back by itself; typing or moving your mouse always comes first.
config.instant_replay: Instant replay: keep the last 30 seconds of each stream
config.instant_replay_desc: View + L1 on the TV saves them as a clip in your Videos\TunaStream folder, exactly as the stream looked. Uses up to 900 MB of the PC's memory while streaming, and asks for a full picture every ten seconds, which on a weak Wi-Fi connection can show as a brief hitch.
config.adaptive_fec: Fit packet-loss protection to the connection (recommended)
config.adaptive_fec_desc: Starts at the amount above, then sends less while the device reports a clean connection and more the moment video is lost. A clean connection carries up to a tenth less data; a rough one gets more protection. Turn off to always send exactly the amount above.
config.fec_percentage_desc: Extra data sent with each frame so the picture survives a lost packet. Higher values hide more glitches on a weak connection but use more bandwidth.
config.file_apps_desc: Where your list of apps is kept.
config.file_state_desc: Where paired devices and their permissions are kept.
config.forward_rumble_desc: Send vibration from games to the controller on your device. Use the test on the Troubleshooting page to check it works.
config.game_frame_limit: Match the game's frame rate to the stream (recommended)
config.game_frame_limit_desc: While someone streams, games are capped at the frame rate their device asked for, so every frame the game draws gets sent. This removes the judder caused by the game and the stream running at different speeds. If RivaTuner Statistics Server (RTSS, part of MSI Afterburner) is running, it does the capping, at the exact rate (59.94 included) and on any graphics card; otherwise NVIDIA's own limit is used, to the nearest whole number. Your own limits come back when streaming stops. If you set a Max Frame Rate for all games in NVIDIA's settings yourself, it is left alone.
config.gamepad_desc: Xbox 360 works with the most games and has the most reliable rumble, so it is the best choice if rumble doesn't work. PlayStation 4 adds the touchpad and motion controls. Automatic picks PlayStation 4 for controllers with those, and Xbox 360 for everything else.
config.general_advanced_desc: Logging and commands that run automatically. You can leave these alone.
config.global_prep_cmd_desc: Configure a list of commands to be executed before or after running any application. If any of the specified preparation commands fail, the application launch process will be aborted.
config.global_state_cmd_desc:
Configure a list of commands to be executed when resuming(first client connects when no clients are connected) or pausing(all clients disconnect) any application.
Do commands for resume and Undo command for pause.
Please make sure to clean up any side effects of the commands in the preparation undo commands.
Please note that pause command will not be executed when the session terminates.
config.headless_mode: Give each stream its own screen (recommended)
config.headless_mode_desc: Turn this off to show your own monitor on the device instead, the way most streaming apps do.
config.hevc_mode_desc: A newer video format that gives a sharper picture for the same bandwidth, and is needed for HDR. Automatic offers it when your graphics card supports it.
config.hide_tray_controls: Hide Stop, Restart and Quit in the taskbar icon menu
config.hide_tray_controls_desc: Useful if others use this PC and shouldn't be able to stop streaming from the taskbar.
config.high_resolution_scrolling_desc: Pass fine-grained scrolling from touchpads through to the PC. Turn off if an older program scrolls far too fast.
config.ignore_encoder_probe_failure: Start even if no encoder was found
config.ignore_encoder_probe_failure_desc: Lets TunaStream start when its encoder check fails at launch. Streams may then fail to start.
config.input_advanced_desc: Fine-tuning for controllers, keyboards and mice. The defaults suit almost everyone.
config.install_steam_audio_drivers_desc: If Steam is installed, this will automatically install the Steam Streaming Speakers driver to support 5.1/7.1 surround sound and muting host audio.
config.isolated_virtual_display_option: Keep my mouse off the stream's screen
config.isolated_virtual_display_option_desc: Stops your mouse sliding onto the stream's screen when you move it past the edge of your monitor. Useful when someone else is playing while you use the PC.
config.keep_sink_default_desc: Whether to force selected virtual sink as default (effective when host audio output is disabled).
config.key_repeat_delay_desc: How long, in milliseconds, a held key waits before it starts repeating.
config.key_repeat_frequency_desc: How many times a second a held key repeats. Decimals are allowed.
config.key_rightalt_to_key_win: Right Alt acts as the Windows key
config.key_rightalt_to_key_win_desc: For devices that can't send the Windows key: Right Alt is pressed as the Windows key instead.
config.keyboard_desc: Let devices type on this PC. You can still turn this off for a single device under Devices.
config.lan_encryption_mode_desc: Encrypting stops others on your network from seeing the stream but can make it slightly slower on older devices.
config.legacy_ordering: Keep app order on older clients
config.legacy_ordering_desc: Makes older clients show apps in your order. Turn off if app names show up garbled.
config.limit_framerate: Limit capture to the device's frame rate
config.limit_framerate_desc: Capture only as many frames a second as the device asked for. Turning this off can add lag on some devices.
config.ui_theme_desc: Colours for this page and for TunaReceive on your TVs, which wear this theme unless set to their own. The last four are the seasonal themes, yours to pick any time. Click one to see it; Save keeps it.
config.locale_desc: The language of this web interface.
config.max_bitrate_desc: The maximum bitrate (in Kbps) that TunaStream will encode the stream at. If set to 0, it will always use the bitrate requested by the client.
config.min_log_level: How much to write to the log
config.min_log_level_desc: More detail helps when tracking down a problem; Info is right for everyday use.
config.min_threads_desc: Only for the software encoder. Raise it a little if the stream stutters while the CPU isn't fully used.
config.minimum_fps_target_desc: The lowest effective FPS a stream can reach. Set 0 for automatic.
config.motion_as_ds4: Use PlayStation 4 for controllers with motion controls
config.motion_as_ds4_desc: When the type is Automatic, a controller with motion sensors is shown to games as a PlayStation 4 controller so motion controls work. Off by default: Xbox-style controllers with a gyro, such as 8BitDo and Switch Pro controllers, then stay Xbox 360, which rumbles more reliably. PlayStation controllers are still recognised by their touchpad.
config.mouse_desc: Let devices move the mouse and use touch on this PC. You can still turn this off for a single device under Devices.
config.native_pen_touch_desc: Pass pen and touch input through as real pen and touch. Turn off if an older program doesn't respond to touch.
config.network_advanced_desc: Settings for unusual networks. The defaults suit almost everyone.
config.notify_pre_releases: Tell me about test versions too
config.notify_pre_releases_desc: Also offer early versions that are still being tested. Leave off unless you want to try new things first.
config.nvenc_h264_cavlc: Prefer CAVLC over CABAC in H.264
config.nvenc_h264_cavlc_desc: Simpler form of entropy coding. CAVLC needs around 10% more bitrate for same quality. Only relevant for really old decoding devices.
config.nvenc_intra_refresh_desc: Enable Intra Refresh for some clients to render correctly continuously (e.g. Xbox Client)
config.nvenc_latency_over_power: Prefer lower encoding latency over power savings
config.nvenc_latency_over_power_desc: TunaStream requests maximum GPU clock speed while streaming to reduce encoding latency. Disabling it is not recommended since this can lead to significantly increased encoding latency.
config.nvenc_opengl_vulkan_on_dxgi: Present OpenGL/Vulkan on top of DXGI
config.nvenc_opengl_vulkan_on_dxgi_desc: TunaStream can't capture full-screen OpenGL and Vulkan games at full frame rate unless they present through DXGI. This setting applies to the whole PC and is put back when TunaStream closes.
config.nvenc_preset_desc: How much effort the graphics card spends on each frame. More effort gives a cleaner picture at the same bitrate, for a little extra delay. Automatic picks what your card can do comfortably.
config.nvenc_realtime_hags: Use realtime priority with hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling
config.nvenc_realtime_hags_desc: Some NVIDIA drivers can freeze the encoder when hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling (HAGS) is on, realtime priority is used and graphics memory is nearly full. Turning this off uses high priority instead, which avoids the freeze but can capture less smoothly when the graphics card is very busy.
config.nvenc_split_frame: Encode each frame in halves at once
config.nvenc_split_frame_desc: Graphics cards with more than one video encoder, such as the RTX 5080, encode the top and bottom of each frame at the same time. TunaStream checks how many the card has. A 4K frame is ready in about half the time, with a quality cost under 2%. Used for HEVC and AV1 above 1440p, with an up-to-date NVIDIA driver. If the encoder turns it down, streaming carries on the usual way.
config.nvenc_spatial_aq: Spend bits where the eye notices (spatial AQ)
config.nvenc_spatial_aq_desc: Spends more of the bitrate where your eye notices: dark scenes, skies and smooth gradients. Less banding and blockiness at the same bitrate.
config.nvenc_twopass_desc: Looks at each frame once quickly before encoding it, to find movement and share the bitrate across the frame. It also keeps each frame within the bitrate, so the connection isn't flooded. Turning it off can cause occasional bursts that show as lost video.
config.nvenc_vbv_increase_desc: By default TunaStream uses single-frame VBV/HRD, which means any encoded video frame size is not expected to exceed requested bitrate divided by requested frame rate. Relaxing this restriction can be beneficial and act as low-latency variable bitrate, but may also lead to packet loss if the network doesn't have buffer headroom to handle bitrate spikes. Maximum accepted value is 400, which corresponds to 5x increased encoded video frame upper size limit.
config.origin_web_ui_allowed: Who can open this settings page
config.origin_web_ui_allowed_desc: Your password is still needed either way. Limiting it to this PC or your home network is safest.
config.output_name_desc_unix: During TunaStream startup, you should see the list of detected displays. Note: You need to use the id value inside the parenthesis. Below is an example; the actual output can be found in the Troubleshooting tab.
config.output_name_desc_windows: Manually specify a display device id to use for capture. If unset, the primary display is captured. Note: If you specified a GPU above, this display must be connected to that GPU. During TunaStream startup, you should see the list of detected displays. Below is an example; the actual output can be found in the Troubleshooting tab.
config.ping_timeout_desc: How long, in milliseconds, to wait without hearing from a device before treating it as disconnected. The game keeps running for two minutes after that so you can reconnect.
config.pkey_desc: The key that goes with the certificate. TunaStream makes one for you; it should be RSA-2048.
config.port_desc: TunaStream uses this port and a few after it, shown below. Change it only if another program needs these ports, such as another streaming host on this PC.
config.port_http_port_note: Use this port when adding this PC by hand in TunaReceive or Moonlight.
config.port_warning: Exposing the Web UI to the internet is a security risk! Proceed at your own risk!
config.qp_desc: Only used by encoders that can't hold a fixed bitrate. Lower numbers mean a better picture and more data.
config.qsv_slow_hevc_desc: This can enable HEVC encoding on older Intel GPUs, at the cost of higher GPU usage and worse performance.
config.restart_note: TunaStream is restarting to apply your changes. This page comes back by itself in a few seconds.
config.screen_intro: When a device starts streaming, TunaStream makes a screen just for it. It is like plugging in an extra monitor that only that device can see.
config.screen_point_monitor: Your own monitor keeps working as normal, so you can use the PC at the same time.
config.screen_point_size: The screen matches the device, so a TV gets a TV-sized picture and a phone gets a phone-sized one.
config.screen_point_stop: When the device stops streaming, the extra screen goes away and your monitor is back to how it was.
config.screen_status_bad: The virtual screen is not working right now, so streams will show your own monitor. Restarting TunaStream usually fixes this; if not, reinstall it.
config.server_cmd_desc: Commands a TV can run from TunaReceive's quick menu (PC commands) during a game. TunaStream adds its own after these: Steam Big Picture, leaving it and restarting Steam (when Steam is installed), and moving the pointer aside.
config.settings_intro: Setup already chose good settings for you. Change things here only if you want to fine-tune something.
config.stream_audio_desc: Turn this off to keep the sound on this PC instead.
config.sw_preset_desc: Optimize the trade-off between encoding speed (encoded frames per second) and compression efficiency (quality per bit in the bitstream). Defaults to superfast.
config.sw_tune_animation: animation -- good for cartoons; uses higher deblocking and more reference frames
config.sw_tune_desc: Tuning options, which are applied after the preset. Defaults to zerolatency.
config.sw_tune_fastdecode: fastdecode -- allows faster decoding by disabling certain filters
config.sw_tune_film: film -- use for high quality movie content; lowers deblocking
config.sw_tune_grain: grain -- preserves the grain structure in old, grainy film material
config.sw_tune_zerolatency: zerolatency -- good for fast encoding and low-latency streaming (default)
config.system_tray: Show the TunaStream icon in the taskbar
config.system_tray_desc: Adds a TunaStream icon next to the clock, with shortcuts to open this page and restart TunaStream.
config.touchpad_as_ds4: Use PlayStation 4 for controllers with a touchpad
config.touchpad_as_ds4_desc: When the type is Automatic, a controller with a touchpad is shown to games as a PlayStation 4 controller so the touchpad works.
config.tunastream_name_desc: The name your devices show for this PC. Leave it empty to use the PC's own name.
config.upnp: Let me play away from home
config.upnp_desc: Asks your router to open the ports TunaStream needs so you can stream over the internet. Your router must support UPnP. Leave off if you only play at home.
config.vaapi_strict_rc_buffer: Strictly enforce frame bitrate limits for H.264/HEVC on AMD GPUs
config.vaapi_strict_rc_buffer_desc: Enabling this option can avoid dropped frames over the network during scene changes, but video quality may be reduced during motion.
config.video_send_rate_desc: How fast each frame is sent. 0 picks it from the stream's bitrate, and from a TV's Wi-Fi link speed when the link is slow, which suits Wi-Fi. Raise it only on a wired 2.5 or 10 gigabit network.
config.virtual_display_only: Never show my monitor on the device (recommended)
config.virtual_display_only_desc: If the stream's own screen can't be made, the stream doesn't start and the device says why, instead of showing everything on your monitor. Turn off to fall back to your monitor.
config.virtual_display_primary: Open games on the stream's screen
config.virtual_display_primary_desc: While someone is streaming, games and new windows open on their screen instead of yours. Turn this off only if games are opening on the wrong screen in a setup you have arranged yourself.
config.virtual_sink_desc:
The audio device to be used when audio output isn't allowed on host by the client.
If unset, the device is chosen automatically.
We strongly recommend leaving this field blank to use automatic device selection!
config.wan_encryption_mode_desc: Encrypting stops others from seeing the stream as it crosses the internet. Leave it on.
config.nvenc_preset_auto: Automatic (default): P5 on RTX 40 and 50 series cards (P4 above 1440p unless frames are split), P1 on older cards
config.ui_theme_seasonal_off: Seasonal themes is now off, so your pick shows instead of {season}. Turn it back on below to wear the seasons again. Save keeps it.
config.restart_slow: TunaStream is taking longer than usual to restart. Reload this page in a moment; if it doesn't come back, check that TunaStream is running on the PC.
config.sharedpc_intro: Keep using this PC while someone streams from it: your screens, sound, mouse and keyboard stay yours, and only the game goes to the TV. Turn Shared PC off for privacy mode instead.
config.privacy_mode: Privacy mode: turn this PC's monitors off while someone streams
config.privacy_mode_desc: Only the stream's own screen stays on, so nobody in the room sees what's being played on the PC. The monitors come back on, as they were arranged, when the stream ends or the TV disconnects. Not available in Shared PC mode, where you're using the monitors. If they ever stay off, press Windows + P and pick Extend.
config.game_vsync_off: Turn Vertical Sync off in games while streaming
config.game_vsync_off_desc: With the cap pacing games, waiting for the screen only adds delay: this takes away up to a frame. NVIDIA graphics cards; your own setting comes back when streaming stops. Turn off if a game shows tearing on the TV.
config.everyday_intro: The settings people change most, in one place. Everything here is also on its own tab, with the rest.
config.everyday_apps: Games, and keeping them in sync
config.everyday_watch: Watch the stream in this browser

index.controller_hint: What games see this controller as. Most PC games only rumble an Xbox 360 controller; change it under Configuration > Input > Emulated Gamepad Type.
index.recap_empty: Nothing played in the last seven days. Streams show up here when they end.
index.recap_smooth_desc: of the minutes played were smooth: no lost video and few frames arriving late.
index.message_failed: The message couldn't be sent. Check that TunaStream is still running.
index.message_not_shown: Not shown yet. Messages need TunaReceive 0.1.60 or later on the TV.
index.tunahome_asks: TunaHome on {name} asks to show your messages on that TV, whether or not anyone's streaming.
index.quick_edit_label: Your quick messages, one per line
index.quick_edit_hint: One per line, up to eight, 60 characters each. They show here and on the phone page.
index.message_title: Show a message on the TV
index.sounds_hint: OGG, MP3 or WAV, up to 2 MB. A few seconds works best.
index.sounds_title: Play a sound on the TV
index.sounds_too_big: That file is larger than 2 MB. Trim it to a few seconds.
index.fps_note_desc: The game itself is drawing too few frames, so the stream isn't the limit. In the game's settings: turn off V-Sync (TunaStream paces frames itself), turn on DLSS or FSR (Performance mode suits 4K), and turn on frame generation if it has it. If it has a frame-rate limit, set it to {target}.
index.fps_note_title: The game is running at {fps} fps, below the {target} the TV asked for
index.fps_reminder_title: To fix: {app} ran at {fps} fps last time, below {target}
index.fps_reminder_title_4k: To fix: {app} ran at {fps} fps at 4K last time, below {target}
index.captures_where: Kept in {pictures} and {videos}. On the TV, the screenshot and replay shortcuts (View + R1 and View + L1 unless changed in TunaReceive's settings) save them here.
index.milestone_game_night: Game night: three or more playing at once
index.milestone_phone_player: A friend joined with a phone
index.milestone_night_owl: Night owl: still playing after 1 a.m.
index.milestone_early_bird: Early bird: a game before 7 a.m.
index.milestone_streak_7: A whole week in a row
index.milestone_full_rate_4k: Half an hour of 4K at full frame rate
index.milestone_smooth_10: Ten streams in a row without lost video
index.phone_desc: Point your phone's camera at the code to open the Live page: what's playing, controller batteries, messages and sounds for the TV, and End session. Add it to your home screen to open it like an app.
index.phone_note: Your phone needs to be on the same Wi-Fi. The first time, it warns that the page's certificate isn't trusted, as your PC's browser did; that's expected for a page on your own PC. Accept it, then sign in.
index.phone_qr_label: QR code for the Live page
index.highlights_busy: Putting the week's replays together. This can take a minute.
index.highlights_done: Saved as {name}, with the last few seconds of each replay from this week.
index.health_hdr_peak: The TV says it shows HDR up to about {nits} nits.
index.custom_port: TunaStream is using port {port} instead of the default. If your client does not find this PC by itself, add it by hand using this PC's IP address followed by :{port}, for example 192.168.1.20:{port}.
index.description: TunaStream streams this PC's games to your TV, phone or tablet.
index.display_restore_failed: Your monitor did not come back as the main display when the stream ended. Press Windows+P and choose PC screen only, or right-click the desktop, open Display settings and make your monitor the main display.
index.end_session_confirm: Quit {app}? Anyone streaming it will be disconnected.
index.health_bad: Something is making this stream uneven
index.health_device_decode: The device takes {ms} ms to decode each frame, longer than a frame lasts. It can't keep up with this picture size: choose a smaller one in TunaReceive.
index.health_device_figures: On the device: {loss}% of the picture lost, {decode} ms to decode a frame, {latency} ms from arriving to showing. Picture quality {mbps} of {setting} Mbps.
index.health_device_full: Frames are arriving slowly at the device ({pct}% of them) though none are lost yet: the connection is nearly full. TunaReceive turns the picture quality down a little by itself.
index.health_figures: {fps} of {target} FPS, {pc} ms on this PC per frame (worst {pcMax} ms), sent in {send} ms at up to {rate} Mbps. Encoding at {mbps} Mbps, with {fec}% packet-loss protection.
index.health_game_slow: Only about {fps} new frames a second reach the stream, out of {target}, while the picture is changing. The game is running slower than the stream: lower its graphics settings, or stream at a lower frame rate.
index.health_measuring: Measuring how smoothly this stream runs…
index.health_network: The device lost video {n} times in the last few seconds and asked for it again. That is the network: move closer to the router, use 5 GHz Wi-Fi or a cable, or lower the picture quality in TunaReceive (or the bitrate in Moonlight).
index.health_network_pc_wifi: This PC is on Wi-Fi itself, so every frame crosses the air twice. A network cable from this PC to the router is the most likely fix.
index.health_ok_desc: Frames are captured, encoded and sent on time. If you still see stutter, it is happening on the network or the device: in TunaReceive, choose Fit picture quality to this connection in the PC's menu, or lower the picture quality.
index.health_pc_slow: The PC takes too long to capture and encode some frames (average {avg} ms, worst {max} ms). Something is keeping the graphics card busy: cap the game's frame rate to leave it room.
index.health_scaled: The device asked for a smaller picture ({pct}% of its usual size) because its connection is struggling. It goes back to full size by itself.
index.health_split: Each frame is encoded on both of the graphics card's video encoders at once, so it is ready in about half the time.
index.health_skipped: The game draws more frames than the stream sends, so about {n} a second are skipped. That shows as judder. Turn on "Match the game's frame rate to the stream" under Settings → Screen and sound, then restart the game. Without an NVIDIA graphics card, cap the game at {target} FPS in its own settings.
index.health_still_desc: Very few new frames are being sent because nothing on the stream's screen is changing, which is normal on the desktop or a paused game. If a moving game looks frozen on the TV, the stream may be showing a different screen than the game: check Troubleshooting → Virtual screen.
index.installed_version_not_stable: You are running a pre-release version of TunaStream. You may experience bugs or other issues. Please report any issues you encounter. Thank you for helping to make TunaStream a better software!
index.new_pre_release: A new Pre-Release Version is Available!
index.new_stable: A new Stable Version is Available!
index.other_host_failed: That didn't work. You can stop or start it from Windows' Services app.
index.other_host_paused: {name} is installed but paused. It starts again when Windows restarts.
index.other_host_running: {name} is also running on this PC. Two streaming hosts at once compete for the graphics card, the virtual screen and the controllers, which can cause stutter or failed streams.
index.paused_desc: Nobody is streaming it right now. Play it here moves the game onto this PC's monitor so you can carry on at the PC. Reconnecting from a device after that streams this PC's screen.
index.paused_failed: The game could not be moved. Try End session and start it again on this PC.
index.paused_play_here: Play it here on this PC
index.paused_title: {app} is paused on the stream's screen
index.pc_wifi_24: It also looks like the slower 2.4 GHz band. Connect this PC to the router's 5 GHz network.
index.pc_wifi_desc: Video leaves this PC through {name} (signal {signal}%, {mbps} Mbps). If the TV is on Wi-Fi too, every frame crosses the air twice, which halves what the connection can carry and is the most common cause of stutter. A network cable from this PC to the router is the biggest single improvement.
index.setup_step_client: Install a client on the device you want to play on:
index.setup_step_pair: Add this PC in the client. It shows a PIN; enter that PIN on the pairing page here.
index.setup_step_play: Pick Desktop or a game in the client to start streaming.
index.startup_errors: Attention! TunaStream detected these errors during startup. We STRONGLY RECOMMEND fixing them before streaming.
index.update_confirm: Install the update now? TunaStream restarts while it installs, so anyone streaming is disconnected for about a minute. Your settings and paired devices are kept.
index.update_desc: Installs straight from here. TunaStream restarts on its own, and keeps your settings and paired devices.
index.update_no_restart: TunaStream did not come back after the update. Start it from the Start menu, or run the installer from the release page.
index.update_stage_installing: Installing TunaStream {version}. TunaStream will restart in a moment.
index.update_stage_restarting: Waiting for TunaStream to start again. This page reloads when it is back.
index.update_stage_up_to_date: TunaStream is already up to date.
index.vdisplay_failed: The last stream showed your monitor instead of its own screen, because the virtual screen driver wasn't working.
index.version_dirty: Thank you for helping to make TunaStream a better software!
index.version_latest: You are running the latest version of TunaStream
index.whatsnew_since: Since {version}, the version this browser last saw:
index.watch_note: Anyone watching signs in with your TunaStream password, or a watch password, or a one-time link you make on the Watch page (Share). Phones need to be on your home Wi-Fi.
index.watch_now_screen: Now: your PC's screen (Share my screen is on).
index.watch_qr_label: QR code for the Watch page
index.watch_when: It goes live when a TV streams a game, or when you share your screen. Open the page now and it starts by itself.
index.sharing_on: Your screen is being shared with browsers watching, for {minutes} more minutes ({viewers} watching now).

password.new_username_desc: If not specified, the username will not change
password.success_msg: Password has been changed successfully! This page will reload soon, your browser will ask you for the new credentials.

pin.playtime_desc: A daily limit for each device, in minutes; leave it at 0 for none. The TV is warned at 10, 5 and 1 minute left, then the game closes, and the device can't start another stream until tomorrow, unless you give it more time here or on the home page.
pin.allow_client_commands_desc: Allow client commands to be executed when connecting to this device.
pin.always_use_virtual_display_desc: Always create a virtual display when connecting from this device.
pin.client_do_cmd_desc: Commands to be executed when client connects. All of the commands are executed detached.
pin.client_undo_cmd_desc: Commands to be executed when client disconnects. All of the commands are executed detached.
pin.display_mode_override_desc: TunaStream will ignore client requested display mode and use this value to configure (virtual) displays. Leave blank for auto matching. Format: [Width]x[Height]x[FPS]
pin.enable_legacy_ordering_desc: Enable app ordering for legacy clients. Disable if this client can't handle UTF8 correctly. Needs to enable "App ordering for legacy clients" in the Advanced settings.
pin.pair_failure: Pairing Failed: Check if the PIN is typed correctly
pin.pair_success: Paired. Go back to your device to continue.
pin.pair_success_check_perm: Pair success! Please grant necessary permissions to the client manually below.
pin.page_desc: Pair a new device, or change what a paired device is allowed to do.
pin.warning_msg: Make sure you have access to the client you are pairing with. This software can give total control to your computer, so be careful!
pin.otp_expired_msg: OTP expired. Please request a new one.
pin.otp_success: PIN request success, the PIN is available within 3 minutes.
pin.otp_msg: One-time codes work with TunaReceive and Artemis. For Moonlight, pair with a PIN.
pin.otp_pair_now: PIN generated successfully, do you want to pair now?
pin.device_management_desc: Manage your paired devices and their permissions.
pin.device_management_warning: The first paired device will have full permissions by default. Other newly paired devices will have limited permissions set by default.
pin.unpair_single_success: However, the device(s) may still be in an active session. Use the 'Force Close' button above to end any open sessions.

resource_card.legal_desc: By continuing to use this software you agree to the terms and conditions in the following documents.
resource_card.resources_desc: Help with common problems, and where to report new ones.

setup.away_away_desc: TunaStream asks your router to let streams in from the internet. Your router must support UPnP.
setup.away_home_desc: Devices on your home network only. The simplest and safest choice.
setup.away_lead: For example on your phone at a friend's place, over mobile data or someone else's Wi-Fi.
setup.away_title: Will you play away from home?
setup.controller_lead: Pick the controller held by whoever is playing. Games on this PC see a controller they understand, and rumble is passed back to it.
setup.controller_none_desc: Touch screen, or a mouse and keyboard
setup.controller_other_desc: A phone clip-on controller or anything else
setup.controller_ps_buttons_desc: Games show ✕ ○ △ □ and the touchpad works. Turn off if rumble doesn't work; games will then show Xbox buttons.
setup.controller_xbox_desc: Xbox One, Xbox Series, Xbox 360, or one with the same layout, such as an 8BitDo Ultimate
setup.device_computer_desc: A laptop or PC elsewhere in the house
setup.device_computer_tip: Pick the resolution of that computer's screen.
setup.device_handheld_desc: Steam Deck, ROG Ally, Legion Go and similar
setup.device_handheld_tip: 1280 × 800 suits the Steam Deck. On other handhelds, pick their own resolution.
setup.device_lead: Pick every kind of device you'll stream to. TunaStream makes a screen that fits each one; this tells you what to choose in the app on it.
setup.device_phone_desc: Android or iPhone, with or without a controller
setup.device_phone_tip: Pick your phone's own resolution (Native). 120 FPS works if your phone's screen supports it.
setup.device_tv1080_tip: Use a wired connection or 5 GHz Wi-Fi for the box connected to the TV.
setup.device_tv4k_desc: Through a streaming box, smart TV app or console
setup.device_tv4k_tip: Turn on HDR in the app on the TV if your TV supports it. A wired connection gives the best picture at 4K.
setup.done_pair: Next, pair the device you'll play on so it can connect.
setup.done_paired: Your settings are saved. Your paired devices can start streaming now.
setup.intro_change: You can run this again any time from Settings.
setup.intro_lead: A few quick questions about how you'll play, and TunaStream sets itself up to match. It takes about a minute.
setup.moonlight_lead: TunaReceive asks for these when it first opens. In Moonlight, open its settings and choose:
setup.moonlight_title: Set up the app on each device
setup.moonlight_wifi: On Wi-Fi, if the picture stutters or breaks up, lower the bitrate first, then the resolution.
setup.review_lead: TunaStream will use these settings. Check them, then save.
setup.save_failed: The settings could not be saved. Check that TunaStream is running and try again.
setup.screen_driver_problem: The virtual screen driver isn't working right now, so streams will show your monitor until it's fixed. You can still choose this: after setup, press Repair virtual screen on the Troubleshooting page.
setup.screen_lead: For example, working at the PC while someone else plays on the TV.
setup.screen_mirror_desc: The stream shows exactly what's on your monitor. Best if nobody uses the PC while you stream.
setup.screen_own: Yes, give the stream its own screen
setup.screen_own_desc: The stream gets an invisible extra screen sized for the device. Games open there and your mouse stays off it, so your monitor is yours.
setup.screen_title: Will you use this PC while someone streams?
setup.skip: Skip, I'll set it up myself
setup.stop_close: Quit it, like closing the game
setup.stop_close_desc: Frees up the PC straight away. Anything not saved in the game is lost. Best if you use the PC while others play.
setup.stop_keep_desc: Reconnect and you're right where you left off, or press Play it here on the home page to carry on at this PC. The game keeps using the graphics card until it's closed.
setup.stop_lead: This is only about closing the stream on purpose. If the Wi-Fi drops by accident, the game always waits two minutes so you can reconnect.
setup.stop_title: When someone closes the stream, what should happen to the game on this PC?
setup.sum_away: Streaming works at home and over the internet.
setup.sum_controller_ps: Controllers show up in games as a PlayStation controller, with rumble and the touchpad.
setup.sum_controller_xbox: Controllers show up in games as an Xbox controller, with rumble.
setup.sum_frame_limit: Games are capped at the stream's frame rate, for smooth video (NVIDIA graphics cards).
setup.sum_home: Streaming works on your home network.
setup.sum_no_controller: Controllers still work if you plug one in later.
setup.sum_screen_own: Each stream gets its own screen, and your mouse stays on your monitor.
setup.sum_stop_close: Games quit when the last person closes the stream.
setup.sum_stop_keep: Games stay open when someone closes the stream, so they can pick up where they left off.

troubleshooting.backup_desc: One file with your settings, apps, sounds, play history and milestones, to keep somewhere safe or move to another PC.
troubleshooting.backup_pairings: Include pairings and sign-in (devices won't need pairing again after a restore)
troubleshooting.backup_pairings_warning: This backup holds the keys your devices trust and your sign-in for this page. Anyone with the file could pretend to be this PC to your devices. Keep it private.
troubleshooting.receiver_backups_desc: TunaReceive can save its settings here, and get them back on a new TV from its Settings.
troubleshooting.restore_confirm: Restore this backup? Its settings replace the current ones, and TunaStream restarts, which ends any stream.
troubleshooting.restore_desc: Pick a backup file made here. TunaStream restarts afterwards.
troubleshooting.restore_done: Restored. TunaStream is restarting; this page reloads in a few seconds.
troubleshooting.wifi_change: Channel {ch} is quieter. Change it in your router's settings (usually under Wireless, then Channel); the PC and TV reconnect by themselves.
troubleshooting.wifi_current: This PC is on channel {ch} ({band} GHz), with {n} other networks heard on that band.
troubleshooting.wifi_desc: Lists the Wi-Fi networks this PC can hear and which channel is quietest. Neighbours on the same channel are a common cause of stutter. The TV may hear a few different ones from where it is.
troubleshooting.wifi_fine: Your channel is as quiet as any. Nothing to change.
troubleshooting.wifi_no_adapter: This PC has no Wi-Fi adapter, so it can't look. On a cable it doesn't need to.
troubleshooting.wifi_not_connected: This PC isn't on Wi-Fi right now (it heard {n} networks). On a cable, the channel only matters for the TV.
troubleshooting.wifi_6ghz: This PC is on channel {ch} at 6 GHz, which few neighbours use yet. Nothing to change.
troubleshooting.wifi_streaming: Someone is streaming, so this shows the last scan instead of making a new one (a scan would interrupt the stream).
troubleshooting.wifi_use_5: This PC is on 2.4 GHz, which is slow and crowded. If your router has 5 GHz, connect the PC to that instead; it makes the biggest difference.
troubleshooting.dd_reset_desc: TunaStream remembers how your displays were set up so it can put them back after a stream. If it keeps trying to put back an old arrangement, forget it here and set your displays up yourself in Windows.
troubleshooting.dd_reset_error: The saved display changes couldn't be forgotten.
troubleshooting.dd_reset_success: Forgotten. TunaStream won't try to put the old arrangement back.
troubleshooting.force_close_desc: If a device says a game is already running and won't let you start another, end it here. This also reloads the app list.
troubleshooting.logs_desc: What TunaStream has been doing, newest at the bottom.
troubleshooting.quit_tunastream_confirm: Quit TunaStream? Devices won't be able to stream until it's started again from the Start menu.
troubleshooting.quit_tunastream_desc: Stops TunaStream and ends any stream. Start it again from the Start menu.
troubleshooting.restart_tunastream_desc: If something isn't working, restarting often fixes it. Any stream ends.
troubleshooting.rumble_test_desc: Rumbles the controllers on every device that's streaming right now, for under a second. It skips the game, so it shows whether rumble can reach the controller at all. If this works but a game doesn't rumble, set the controller type the PC sees to Xbox 360 in Settings > Controls and reconnect: most PC games only rumble an Xbox controller. If this does nothing, check the controller on the device: in TunaReceive, Settings > Check my controller.
troubleshooting.rumble_test_none: No device is streaming. Start a stream with a controller connected, then try again.
troubleshooting.rumble_test_sent: Rumble sent to {count} streaming device(s). The controller should have buzzed.
troubleshooting.vdisplay_desc: The virtual screen driver makes the invisible extra screen each stream plays on. If it stops working, streams show your monitor instead.
troubleshooting.vdisplay_reason_failed: The driver is missing, turned off in Device Manager, or in use by another program. Apollo and programs based on it use the same driver: quit them first. Then press Repair.
troubleshooting.vdisplay_reason_unknown: TunaStream connects to the driver when it starts or when a stream begins.
troubleshooting.vdisplay_reason_version: Another program installed a version of the driver TunaStream can't use. Repair puts back the version that comes with TunaStream.
troubleshooting.vdisplay_reason_watchdog: This often happens after the PC wakes from sleep. Repair reconnects to it.
troubleshooting.vdisplay_repair_failed: The repair could not be started. Restart TunaStream and try again.
troubleshooting.vdisplay_repair_note: Reinstalls the driver that comes with TunaStream and reconnects to it. Takes up to a minute; can't run while someone is streaming. If it still fails, restart the PC.
troubleshooting.vdisplay_repairing: Reinstalling and reconnecting the driver. Your screens may flicker for a moment…
troubleshooting.tv_logs_desc: When something goes wrong on a TV, open TunaReceive, pick this PC, then PC tools > Send logs to PC. The log appears here, so it can be read or shared without connecting anything to the TV.
troubleshooting.tv_logs_gone: That log isn't on this PC any more.
troubleshooting.checklist_link: Trying new features? Use the test checklist.

tvset.title: TV settings
tvset.desc: Change TunaReceive's settings on a TV from here, where there's room to explain them. While TunaReceive shows its games, the TV shares its settings and picks up your changes within 15 seconds; otherwise it picks them up the next time it opens. Changes are used from the next game.
tvset.none: No TV has shared its settings yet. Update TunaReceive on the TV (v0.1.70 or newer) and open it once.
tvset.profile: The profile "{profile}" is in use on this TV. Settings the profile sets override these until another profile is picked.
tvset.waiting: {n} change(s) waiting for the TV. Open TunaReceive on it (its games screen) to pick them up.
tvset.clash: {other} uses the same buttons; the TV will turn that one off.
tvset.sent: Sent. The TV picks them up within 15 seconds while its games are on screen, and shows which ones changed.
tvset.more_list_resolution: Pick your TV's own size (4K on a 4K TV) for the sharpest picture; the PC's virtual screen is made at this size, so games run at it too. With "Adjust picture size too" on, the stream drops lower by itself when the Wi-Fi can't keep up.
tvset.more_list_fps: A game that can't reach this rate looks less smooth, not broken: the stream details (View + R3) show what the game itself draws.
tvset.more_seekbar_bitrate_kbps: This is the most the stream may use; with "Adjust picture quality to the Wi-Fi" on it goes lower when needed. On a good 5 GHz connection 80 to 150 Mbps suits 4K at 60 fps; over a weak connection, start around 40.
tvset.more_tuna_adaptive_quality: Recommended on Wi-Fi. Off keeps the bitrate fixed, which can stutter when the network is busy.
tvset.more_checkbox_enable_hdr: Windows' HDR is turned on for the stream's virtual screen while the TV is connected.
tvset.more_tuna_10bit: Needs HEVC or AV1; on the Shield the stream uses HEVC.
tvset.more_checkbox_use_virtual_display: Off streams the PC's own main monitor instead, at its size.
tvset.more_tuna_shortcut_menu: The quick menu has the screenshot, replay, stream details, keyboard, and ending the stream.
tvset.more_tuna_shortcut_screenshot: Saved on the TV and in Pictures\TunaStream on the PC.
tvset.more_tuna_shortcut_replay: Saved in Videos\TunaStream on the PC. Needs Instant replay on under Settings > General.
tvset.more_tuna_shortcut_stats: Picture size, frame rate (set, now, average and what the game draws), delay, how steady the stream is, bitrate and the TV's Wi-Fi.
tvset.more_tuna_shortcut_quit: The game keeps running on the PC, so you can pick up where you left off.
tvset.more_checkbox_enable_perf_overlay: The stream details shortcut shows more, only when you want it.
tvset.more_list_languages: Used the next time TunaReceive opens.
tvset.more_tuna_checkup_before_game: It suggests a picture size, frame rate and bitrate that suit the connection and the TV, plus turning off HDR or 10-bit where the TV can't use them; each one can be taken or left, and the game starts either way.

checklist.title: Test checklist
checklist.self_cheer: Show a test cheer on this PC
checklist.self_cheer_look: Look at the bottom right of the PC's main screen: a 👋 card should show for a few seconds.
checklist.self_desc: What this PC can check by itself. A warning explains what won't work and why.
checklist.self_service_ok: TunaStream runs as a service, so it works before anyone signs in.
checklist.self_service_info: TunaStream runs as you, not as a service: it stops when you sign out.
checklist.self_signed_in_ok: Someone is signed in, so WGC, game sound only and the helpers can run.
checklist.self_signed_in_warn: Nobody is signed in: WGC and game sound only wait until someone signs in.
checklist.self_windows_ok: Windows build {detail}: game sound only can leave out voice chat.
checklist.self_windows_warn: Windows build {detail} is older than Windows 10 2004: game sound only isn't available, so viewers hear everything.
checklist.self_capture_ok: Screen capture: Windows.Graphics.Capture, through the helper in your session.
checklist.self_capture_warn: Screen capture is set to WGC, but nobody is signed in: Desktop Duplication is used until someone does.
checklist.self_capture_info: Screen capture: {detail} (Desktop Duplication). Try WGC under Settings > Video encoding.
checklist.self_second_encoder_ok: The graphics card can encode a second picture: Watch and Share my screen work while a TV plays.
checklist.self_second_encoder_warn: This PC's encoder can't make a second picture at the same time: Watch and Share my screen won't work.
checklist.self_virtual_display_ok: The virtual display driver is working.
checklist.self_virtual_display_warn: The virtual display driver isn't working (code {detail}). Troubleshooting > Repair the virtual display fixes this.
checklist.self_rtss_ok: RivaTuner Statistics Server is running: frame caps are exact, 59.94 included.
checklist.self_rtss_warn: RivaTuner Statistics Server is installed but not running: start it for exact frame caps.
checklist.self_rtss_info: RivaTuner Statistics Server isn't installed: NVIDIA's frame cap is used, rounded to whole numbers.
checklist.self_wake_ok: {detail} is wired and allowed to wake this PC, so the TV can wake it from sleep.
checklist.self_wake_warn: {detail} isn't allowed to wake this PC, so the TV can't wake it. In Device Manager, open this network adapter's Properties > Power Management and tick "Allow this device to wake the computer" and "Only allow a magic packet to wake the computer". Wake-on-LAN may also need switching on in the BIOS.
checklist.self_wake_info: This PC is on Wi-Fi ({detail}): most PCs can't be woken over Wi-Fi. Use a network cable if you want to wake it from the TV.
checklist.self_fast_startup_info: Windows Fast startup is on: the TV can wake this PC from sleep, but usually not once it's shut down. To wake it from shut down too, switch off Fast startup (Control Panel > Power Options > Choose what the power buttons do).

checklist.note_placeholder: What you saw, and what you were doing

privacy.title: Privacy mode
privacy.how: Turn off Settings > Shared PC > Shared PC, turn on Privacy mode, and save. Then start a game on the TV.
privacy.expect: The PC's monitors go dark while the TV streams, and come back on when the stream ends.

quiet.title: No notifications during a stream
quiet.how: Start a stream, then make something show a Windows notification (a Discord message, for example).
quiet.expect: Nothing pops up over the game, and notifications show again once the stream ends.

borderless.title: Borderless games
borderless.how: With Shared PC on, start a game that normally opens fullscreen.
borderless.expect: It opens as a borderless window on the TV's screen, and the PC's own screen is left alone.

apply.title: Saving without signing in again
apply.how: Change any setting on this page, then Save and Apply.
apply.expect: The page waits while TunaStream restarts and comes back without asking you to sign in.

theme.title: Theme
theme.how: Pick another theme under Settings > General and save.
theme.expect: This page changes and stays changed after Apply. TunaReceive matches it the next time it opens.

remote.title: TV settings from this PC
remote.how: Open the Devices page, change something under TV settings, and save. The TV needs TunaReceive open.
remote.expect: The TV shows the new value within about 15 seconds.

phone.title: Phone page
phone.how: During a stream, open this PC's address followed by /live on a phone on the same network.
phone.expect: It shows what's playing, with the same details as the TV's stream details.

logs.title: Send logs to PC
logs.how: On the TV, open this PC, then PC tools > Send logs to PC.
logs.expect: The TV says it was sent, and the log appears under Troubleshooting > Logs from TVs.

checkup.title: Check before a game
checkup.how: On the TV, start a game (the check is on unless it was turned off in Settings).
checkup.expect: It measures for a few seconds, then starts the game or offers changes. Use checked, Use all and Keep mine each do what they say.

overlay.title: Stream details
overlay.how: During a stream, press View + right stick (or the buttons set under Settings > Controller shortcuts).
overlay.expect: Picture size, frame rate, Wi-Fi and delay show over the game. Pressing again hides them.

shortcuts.title: Changing a shortcut
shortcuts.how: On the TV, open Settings > Controller shortcuts, pick one, choose Press new buttons, and press a combination.
shortcuts.expect: The new buttons work during a game, and Back to how it came puts the old ones back.

gameprofile.title: Settings for each game
gameprofile.how: On the TV, save a settings profile, then hold a game and choose Settings for this game. Start that game, then a different one.
gameprofile.expect: The first says it's using the profile. The other uses your usual settings.

sharpen.title: Sharpen the picture
sharpen.how: On the TV, set Settings > Sharpen the picture to Medium and stream at 1080p. Then try Off to compare.
sharpen.expect: Edges and text look crisper without bright outlines, and the game doesn't feel slower.

drift.title: Fix stick drift
drift.how: On the TV, turn on Settings > Fix stick drift. Use a controller whose camera or character creeps, and let go of the stick for two seconds.
drift.expect: The creeping stops, and small stick movements still count.

ntsc.title: 59.94 FPS
ntsc.how: On the TV, set Frame rate to 59.94 FPS, stream a game, and pan the camera slowly. Open stream details.
ntsc.expect: Panning stays smooth without a hitch every few seconds, and stream details shows about 59.9 FPS.

whatsnew.title: What's new
whatsnew.how: After the next update, open TunaReceive and this page.
whatsnew.expect: Each shows what changed once, and not again.

everyday.title: Everyday settings
everyday.how: Open Settings. It should open on the Everyday tab. Change one setting there and save.
everyday.expect: The tab shows the settings most people change, grouped, with links to games, devices and fixes. The change is kept after reloading the page.

watch.title: Watch in a browser
watch.how: While the TV streams a game, open the Watch page from the dashboard on a laptop or phone on the same network and tap Sound on.
watch.expect: The game appears within a few seconds with sound, a little behind the TV. The TV's picture and controls aren't affected.

watchlink.title: Watch link
watchlink.how: On the Watch page, choose Share a watch link and open the copied link on a tablet that isn't signed in. Open the same link again on a second device. The next day, open Watch on the tablet again.
watchlink.expect: The tablet watches without the password and can't open any other page. The second device is told the link was already used. The tablet keeps working the next day, and Change Password > Access tokens lists it as a watch key that changes daily; removing it stops it.

watchpassword.title: Watch password
watchpassword.how: On the Watch page, make a watch password for someone. On a tablet that isn't signed in, open the Watch page and type it. Then type a wrong one five times on another device.
watchpassword.expect: The tablet watches without a link. The password keeps working on later days. After five wrong tries, that device is told to wait ten minutes. Removing the password under Access tokens stops the tablet too.

watchers.title: Who's watching
watchers.how: While someone watches through a watch link or password, open Watch on the PC signed in. Switch Picture to Sharper, then choose Remove access for that viewer.
watchers.expect: The list shows them by name and device. Their picture comes back sharper after a few seconds. After Remove access their device stops and asks for a new link or password.

cheers.title: Cheers
cheers.how: While someone watches your shared screen, they tap 🔥 on the Watch page. Then do the same while a TV streams. Finally turn off Let viewers send cheers.
cheers.expect: The cheer pops up in the corner of your shared screen for a few seconds (and in their picture), and on the TV as a message while it streams. Other viewers see it too. With cheers off, the buttons say they're turned off.

watchtv.title: Watch on a TV
watchtv.how: While one TV streams a game, on a second TV with TunaReceive press and hold the PC and choose Watch. Then end the stream on the first TV.
watchtv.expect: The second TV shows the game with sound within a few seconds, a little behind, and can't control anything. When the stream ends it says so and waits for the next one.

sharescreen.title: Share my screen
sharescreen.how: With no TV streaming, open Watch on the PC, choose Share my screen for 1 hour, and open a watch link on a tablet. Then start a stream on the TV, end it, and finally choose Stop sharing.
sharescreen.expect: The tablet shows the PC's main screen with sound; the home page and the tray say it's being shared. When the TV streams the tablet shows the TV's game, then the PC's screen again. After Stop sharing the tablet waits.

gamesound.title: Game sound only
gamesound.how: Share your screen with Discord voice chat going, set Sound to Everything except Discord, and listen on the tablet.
gamesound.expect: The tablet hears the game but not the voice chat. Switching back to Everything brings the voice chat back after a few seconds.

sharewindow.title: Share one window
sharewindow.how: On the Watch page, under Share my screen, pick a game's window from the list and share it. Make the window smaller, switch to another window on the PC, then close the game.
sharewindow.expect: The tablet shows only the game's window, filling the picture whatever its size, and hears only the game, even while you're in another window. When the game closes, sharing stops; the rest of the screen is never shown.

wakepc.title: Wake the PC from the TV
wakepc.how: Put the PC to sleep (Start > Power > Sleep). On the TV, open TunaReceive and select the PC. First check the Self-check above: it says whether this PC's network adapter is allowed to wake it.
wakepc.expect: "Waking" shows on the TV, the PC wakes within about 30 seconds, and its games open by themselves. If it doesn't wake, the TV says what the PC needs.

signin.title: Keep me signed in
signin.how: Sign out, then sign in with Keep me signed in turned on. Close the browser and open the dashboard again. Repeat with it turned off.
signin.expect: With it on you stay signed in after closing the browser; with it off you're asked for the password again.

tokens.title: Access tokens
tokens.how: Under Change Password > Access tokens, make a token that can only see what's playing and copy it. Remove it afterwards.
tokens.expect: The token is shown once. Removing it makes it stop working straight away.

librarysync.title: Keep my games in sync
librarysync.how: On Apps, turn on Keep my games in sync and choose Sync now. Then delete one of the synced games.
librarysync.expect: Games played recently appear with covers and a Synced badge. Games you added yourself aren't touched, and the deleted game doesn't come back.

framecap.title: Exact frame cap
framecap.how: With RivaTuner Statistics Server installed and Match the game's frame rate on, stream a game at 59.94 or 119.88 FPS and check RTSS's limit. End the stream.
framecap.expect: RTSS shows the stream's exact rate while streaming, and its own limit is back afterwards. Without RTSS, NVIDIA's frame cap is used as before.

vsync.title: V-Sync off while streaming
vsync.how: On an NVIDIA PC, keep Turn Vertical Sync off in games while streaming on, stream a game that uses V-Sync, then end the stream.
vsync.expect: The game feels as responsive as without V-Sync while streaming, and the NVIDIA setting is back to how it was afterwards.

wgc.title: Windows.Graphics.Capture
wgc.how: Under Settings > Video encoding, set Screen capture method to Windows.Graphics.Capture and save. Stream a game, then press Win+L or open a UAC prompt on the PC, and go back.
wgc.expect: The stream works, the lock screen or UAC prompt shows on the TV, and the game comes back when it closes. If anything looks wrong, set it back to Automatic.

watch.ended: The stream ended. Watching starts again by itself when someone plays.

watch.no_sound_here: Watch only. This browser can't play the sound; try Chrome or Edge.

watch.screen_desc: While no TV is streaming, browsers watching (with this page or a watch link) see this PC's main screen and hear its sound. When a TV starts streaming they see its game instead. It turns itself off after the time you choose.
watch.screen_on: Your screen is shared for {minutes} more minutes.
watch.need_link: This device can't watch yet. Open a new watch link from the person who shares, or sign in.
watch.share_windows: Just one window, with its sound

watch.cheers_allow: Let viewers send cheers (they pop up on your screen while you share it, or on the TV while it streams)

watch.home_screen_tip: Tip: Add to Home Screen in the browser's menu opens Watch like an app.
watch.viewers_remove_desc: Remove access stops that device watching. If it got in with a watch password, that password stops working too, on every device.
watch.viewers_remove_confirm: Stop {name} watching and remove its access?
watch.passwords_desc: A watch password doesn't change. Typed on the Watch page of a tablet or phone, it lets that device watch, the same as a watch link. Make one for each person, so you can remove one without the others.

watch.passwords_failed: The watch password couldn't be made.

tokens.desc: Let a script, a Stream Deck, Home Assistant or an AI assistant do a few things without your password. Each token can only do what you tick, and you can remove it any time. To let someone watch, use Share a watch link on the Watch page instead: those links work once and the device's key changes daily.
tokens.made_once: Copy it now: it isn't shown again.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.name_placeholder: Watch link for the living room
tokens.scope_status: See what's playing and the devices
tokens.scope_messages: Send messages and sounds to TVs
tokens.scope_sessions: End sessions and give more play time
tokens.scope_logs: Read TunaStream's log and logs sent from TVs
tokens.agent_desc: Claude Desktop, Claude Code and other assistants that use MCP can run TunaStream as a tool with this token. Paste this into the assistant's MCP settings (for Claude Desktop: Settings > Developer > Edit Config), then restart the assistant. It can do only what this token allows.
tokens.remove_confirm: Remove {name}? Anything using it stops working.
